newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-INJURIES FORCE TOP AMERICANS OUT OF GRAND SLAM CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-INJURIES FORCE TOP AMERICANS OUT OF GRAND SLAM CUP.

text.p: Top Americans Pete Sampras, the world number one, Todd Martin and Michael Chang have all pulled out of the lucrative Grand Slam Cup starting in Munich on Tuesday, citing injury.
Grand Slam administrator Bill Babcock, in Malmo for the Davis Cup final, said Martin had a long-standing elbow injury.
Sampras and Chang's medical reports said they were suffering from tendinitis, both with sore ankles.
Babcock said that the crowded end-of-year tennis calendar was bound to result in top players finishing the season with nagging injuries.

Sweden's Thomas Enqvist, who won a punishing five-set match against Cedric Pioline in the Davis Cup final here on Sunday, comes in to the Grand Slam Cup draw alongside Britain's Tim Henman and Swiss Jakob Hlasek as replacements.
Enqvist and Pioline, who was in the original draw, play their first matches on Wednesday.

Draw: Michael Stich (Germany) v Tim Henman (Britain), MaliVai Washington (U.S) v Richard Krajicek (Netherlands), Boris Becker (Germany) v Jason Stoltenberg (Australia), Jakob Hlasek (Switzerland) v Cedric Pioline (France), Marc Rosset (Switzerland) v Jim Courier (U.S.), Thomas Enqvist (Sweden) v Yevgeny Kafelnikov (Russia), Andre Agassi (U.S.) v Mark Woodforde (Australia), Mikael Tillstrom (Sweden) v Goran Ivanisevic (Croatia).
